source.title: Built on Borrowed Time
source.summary: The bond market contains the seeds of its own destruction. A system built on riba is a system built on borrowed time. The Quran warned us. The math confirms it.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: US federal interest payments now exceed defense spending at $1.1 trillion per year. The government borrows to pay interest on previous borrowing. Japan's debt is 260% of GDP. The system needs perpetual growth just to service existing debt, and that growth is slowing. Gold has surged, central banks are quietly losing faith, and bilateral trade agreements bypass the dollar. The Quran describes those who consume riba as unable to stand straight, an image of instability and madness. The hadith warned that riba's dust would reach everyone. Islamic scholars weren't just making moral points; they were describing a mathematical flaw. This finale ties the entire series together: the bond market isn't just a financial system. It's a civilizational choice. And a civilization built on debt is a civilization built on borrowed time.
